label: first original token is f (t=0)
explanation: Fires only at step 0 when the first input token is the letter f. Magnitude is constant (2.324) on every such step, so nothing modulates it. It does not fire on f at any later position, on other first tokens, or at the delimiter. The copy phase has 3 tiny stray activations (dev split), where the feed-back input is f right after <DEL>.

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0 and F1 1.0, with 0 missed activations and 0 false positives across 16729 active steps.

On the dev split the activation profile shows mean = median = max = 2.324, so the claim of constant magnitude holds. All activations fall at t=0 with in_tok=f. There are 0 activations at the delimiter and at t=1..9. 'f' is the only active in_tok.

The 3 dev misses match the explanation. They occur at t=10 in L=9 sequences that start with f, at the first copy step after <DEL>, where the fed-back input is f. They have tiny activations (0.02 to 0.06 of max) and carry 0.0% of the activation mass, which is negligible noise. Strictly speaking this means 'never in copy phase' is not literally true, but the explanation already discloses it.
